messages:
Jordan - Support: Hey team, escalating a live customer issue. ShopGood is reporting clients dropping mid-SSE stream ~8-15s after starting. They see partial output (first few tokens) then the client gives up. Customer says it spikes on office Wi‑Fi -> phone hotspot switches. Ticket: https://support.example/INC-3421. Logs show nginx 499s and the SDK client logs show ‘stream closed by client’ + no final event. Can someone take a look?

Alex M.: Thanks. I pulled a sample request from the customer: they use the streaming chat endpoint /v1/streams/chat with our JS SDK v0.8.1. Their client log shows: 

```
[12:03:12.123] SDK: opening SSE to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat
[12:03:13.200] SSE: data: {"delta":"Hello"}
[12:03:20.341] SDK: networkchange -> wifi->cellular
[12:03:20.642] SDK: socket closed, reconnecting? status: ECONNRESET
[12:03:20.643] SDK: gave up after 3s
```

And our edge nginx shows: `499 "Client Closed Request"` with the x-request-id header `rq_97a3b` and upstream time ~7.4s.

Sophie (mobile-dev): That pattern looks like the mobile OS tearing down sockets on network handover. On Android that can lead to a TCP RST and apps often see ECONNRESET. If the SDK immediately aborts the stream instead of attempting a short reconnect/resume, the server will log 499. Which matches here.

Mari G. (SRE): I pulled the edge trace for rq_97a3b: route us-east-1/edge-12 -> runtime-node-3, stream started and produced 4 chunks then connection terminated. No server-side error. Upstream response_time 7.41s, request_time 7.42s. So server delivered tokens but TCP closed before finalization.

Jordan - Support: Customer also attached a pcap where I can see a TCP RST from the client after roaming. They asked if we can make streaming resumable—customer uses real-time chat and losing mid-response is a bad UX.

Alex M.: Quick notes: 
- Our current SSE path does not support resume by default (no per-token ack). We can add an idempotency/session token so client can request continuation from last token index, but that's a nontrivial product change.
- Short-term mitigations: SDK should implement a short reconnect/promised-resume window (e.g., 10s) and attempt to reopen the stream and request only missing suffix if server supports it, otherwise re-run prompt with prefix caching.

Sophie (mobile-dev): For the immediate workaround on mobile: 
1) Update SDK to keep a light retry/backoff on ECONNRESET for the first 15s.
2) Increase internal socket keepalive on Android to avoid OS-level aggressive teardown (Socket.setKeepAlive(true, 30)).
3) Ensure app doesn't call `.close()` on networkchange; instead mark as pending and let the reconnect logic attempt to resume.

Example repro curl (non-browser) to mimic stream: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat -d '{"model":"redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
If you kill the TCP flow mid-stream (e.g., `pkill -f curl` or `sudo ifconfig wlan0 down`) you should see 499 on edge.

Mari G. (SRE): Operational action items I suggest: 
- Capture pcap from affected customer's device during a repro (tcpdump -i any port 443 -w sse-repro.pcap).
- Ask for `x-request-id` headers for each failing attempt so we can correlate traces.
- Add short-term alert rule to surface 499 spikes on /v1/streams/* with client ip in mobile ranges.

Jordan - Support: I'll request the pcap and the x-request-id from ShopGood. Also asked them to try our non-SDK curl repro to see if browser behavior differs.

ops-bot: [monitoring] spike detected: 120% increase in 499s on /v1/streams/chat in us-east-1 over last 10m. Incident #SR-768 created.

Alex M.: From a product standpoint, two lanes: 
A) Short term (1-2 weeks): mobile SDK patch to retry/hold-resume for ephemeral network flaps + docs recommending `setKeepAlive` and not forcibly closing streams on `CONNECTIVITY_CHANGE`.
B) Medium term (quarter): implement resumable streaming tokens + server-side cache to replay last N tokens for a short window (30s) to allow quick reconnect and continue.

Sophie (mobile-dev): I can cut a v0.8.2 patch with a 10s reconnect window and exponential backoff (200ms -> 400ms -> 800ms) and a telemetry flag to collect reconnect stats (counts + durations). Need eng runtime to add an opt-in header `X-Resume-Window: 10` we can send to signal the server we want a small resume buffer.

Alex M.: We can add `X-Resume-Window` as an incremental opt-in. Runtime will keep the last N tokens in an in-memory slot keyed by session id for that window; if client reconnects with the session id we can attempt to continue rather than treat it as a new stream. I'll scope the safety and memory cost.

Jordan - Support: Next steps for support: 
- Collect pcap + x-request-id from customer.
- Ask them to try SDK nightly with keepalive/retry behavior if they can.
- Offer a short-term tweak: route their tenant to a less-congested edge node if we see pathological wifi NAT behavior.

Mari G. (SRE): Also add this to runbook: if we see 499 bursts correlated with `networkchange` UA substrings (Android WebView/Chrome) then escalate to eng-runtime and mobile SDK owners.

Jordan - Support: I've messaged ShopGood asking for the pcap and attached our curl repro + suggestion to try a hotspot to confirm it's the handover. Will update thread when they reply. :thumbsup:

Sophie (mobile-dev): I'll start the SDK patch PR today and post the branch link.

Alex M.: I'll draft the runtime opt-in header spec and rough implementation plan.

Jordan - Support: Thanks everyone — marking P1 for now until we get repro.
